A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same native multimodal scaling-law study. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable, and retained material can be matched despite extensive reformatting and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original model-training experiments, fitted scaling laws, architecture comparisons, bootstrap analyses, and downstream VQA and captioning results.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results and adds context-length comparisons and downstream evaluations of additional MoE configurations.

M1.justification: The early-fusion, late-fusion, and dropless MoE architectures, training objectives, and default eight-expert top-1 routing remain unchanged. The additional expert-count and routing configurations are presented as ablations rather than revisions to the proposed method.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same image-caption, interleaved, and text datasets and the same downstream VQA and captioning benchmarks. The new context-length and MoE experiments vary configurations within retained data and tasks.

E2.justification: The early/late fusion, dense/sparse, modality-aware/agnostic, and pretrained-initialization comparisons retain their comparator membership. New Table 13 varies configurations of the existing MoE model; newly cited systems such as SmolVLA are not evaluated.

E3.justification: v3 adds 1k-versus-2k context evaluations over 0.1–0.3T training tokens and SFT comparisons using four or eight experts, top-1 or top-2 routing, and a fine-grained variant. Existing experiments retain their stated training protocols and metrics.

E4.justification: Appendix B.6/Figure 20 adds a context-length sensitivity check, and Appendix E.1/Table 13 adds MoE-configuration ablations. Conversely, v1 Figure 22's third, green prediction-fit panel is omitted from v3 Figure 23. The 8B extrapolation and bootstrap analyses are retained after relocation.

E5.justification: The same 100-iteration bootstrap procedure and coefficient means and standard deviations appear in v1 Tables 6/12 and v3 Table 11. The new experiments add no seed counts, confidence intervals, significance tests, or other uncertainty-reporting practices.

E6.justification: The aggregate sparse scaling fit changes from 26.287C^-0.047 in v1 Figure 24 to 27.086C^-0.048 in v3 Figure 26; per-modality sparse fits also change. Context-length curves and four MoE-configuration SFT rows are added, while one prediction-fit panel is removed. Main downstream scores remain identical. v3 Figure 9 still displays the old sparse fit.

T1.justification: The parametric loss law, fitting objective, compute-optimal derivations, sparsity-aware formulation, and specialization definitions are retained. Revised fitted coefficients are empirical results; the new context-length discussion explains an existing compute approximation without changing its mathematics.

C1.justification: Both versions claim similar early/late fusion scaling, greater early-fusion efficiency, and benefits from sparse modality specialization and learned routing. The abstract's added mention of avoiding image tokenizers makes explicit a property already stated in v1.

C2.justification: v3 Figure 12 newly attributes HQITP's higher specialization scores to image/text token imbalance. Appendix B.6 explains the treatment of context length in compute estimates and interprets its sensitivity test. Existing limitations are retained in Appendix D.

D1.justification: v3 documents context lengths, expert counts, and routing choices for the added experiments and supplies an HQITP provenance citation in Table 5. Existing implementation details remain unchanged. The new SFT table leaves its training budget, model size, and fine-grained implementation unspecified.

R1.justification: v3 adds Pearce and Song's scaling-law study, Ranasinghe et al. for HQITP, and SmolVLA, while removing several introductory audio and speech references. Its central positioning relative to native multimodal models, early fusion, and MoEs remains stable.

P1.justification: Most prose and the main narrative are retained. v3 moves scaling-law validation into Appendix C.6, condenses the main limitations section while retaining details in Appendix D, reorganizes the MoE appendix, and shortens related-work prose.

P2.justification: The document undergoes a pervasive two-column redesign with substantial figure and table resizing and relocation. Figure 1 is restacked with expanded axes, validation displays move to the appendix, and duplicate bootstrap tables are consolidated. A context-length figure and configuration table are added, and a prediction-fit panel is removed.

improvement.justification: The context-length test and MoE-configuration ablation provide useful additional checks of previously untested sensitivities, modestly strengthening empirical support. The gain is limited by sparse documentation of the new SFT experiments, removal of one prediction-fit panel, and inconsistent sparse scaling coefficients between v3 Figure 9 and Section 4.2/Figure 26.
